match.reason: The bank point covers accounting treatment of returns, bad debts and discounts, while the new point asks students to distinguish good debt that funds growing assets or income from bad debt that funds depreciating goods, which is a different idea.

draft.title: Good debt and bad debt
card: Debt is money you borrow and must pay back, usually with interest. Interest is the extra amount the lender charges for the loan.
borrowing to pay for something that grows in value or earns income, such as study or a home. It may help you earn or own more later.
borrowing to pay for things that lose value, such as clothes or a gadget. It often has high interest, so you can end up paying much more than the price.
The line is not always clear. A good debt can still cause trouble if the repayments are more than a person can afford.
draft.remember: Good debt buys something that grows in value or earns income. Bad debt buys things that lose value.

a.q: Which loan is the best example of good debt?
opts: A loan to pay for a course that helps you get a better job
A loan to buy a new game console
A loan to pay for a holiday
A loan to buy a party outfit
a.why: A course can raise future income, so the debt pays for something that earns. A console, holiday and outfit lose value or give no lasting return.
a.clue: Which loan might help you earn more later?

b.q: Jo puts a gadget on a store card at a high rate of interest and pays only a little each month. Why is this often bad debt?
opts: The gadget loses value while interest adds to the cost
The gadget grows in value, so the interest is a waste
All borrowing is bad debt, whatever it pays for
Store cards cannot charge interest on a gadget
b.why: A gadget loses value, and high interest means Jo pays far more than the price. Not all borrowing is bad debt, as study or a home may grow in value or earn income.
b.clue: Think about what happens to the gadget's value and to the interest.

a.best: A loan to pay for a course that helps you get a better job

b.best: The gadget loses value while interest adds to the cost

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest and the only one with a qualifying detail ('that helps you get a better job'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea. The other options are short ('a holiday', 'a new game console', 'a party outfit').
